name: verne-trilingual-peer
description: CROSS-LANGUAGE case (BACKLOG B10 + B14): the same three real witnesses as case 22 (Verne '20,000 Leagues' Pt 1 Ch.1 — the French original + the Mercier and Walter English translations), but collated with the PEER-MSA strategy and a TRANSLATION LEXICON covering the passage's skeleton (année/year, marquée/marked/signalised, phénomène/phenomenon, …). Case 22 pinned the honest NEGATIVE: without translation-aware anchoring the graph aligns positionally and drifts. This case pins the B10 fix: lexicon pairs anchor the alignment across the language boundary, each slot shows the per-witness renderings (the synoptic translation view — 'marquée | signalised | marked'), and where the two translations share a rendering they group onto ONE reading against the French. The lexicon is inline in this meta.json, so the case is self-contained and language-neutral. This is the pilot for the collated Verne digital corpus (all French editions + English translations). Residual, documented: French noun-adjective inversions ('phénomène inexpliqué' vs 'mysterious phenomenon') are an alignment tie and may pair one slot off; see CASE_STUDY.md.
